topic: Watertight canonical top-left edge function vs shared-edge seam crack rig
topic_zh: 水密规范端点排序与顶左填充边函数对比共边漏光裂缝
scope: Deterministic Pineda (1988) / Woop (2013) watertight barycentric edge functions with canonical sorted-endpoint evaluation and Top-Left tie-breaking versus naive strict interior testing across 17 shared-seam quad stations. No neural surface reconstruction execution.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Division/sqrt-free canonical sorted-endpoint 2D edge determinant versus Heron 3-subtriangle square-root area evaluation.

protocol.function: e_BA(P) ≡ −e_AB(P), hit ⇔ e > 0 ∨ (e == 0 ∧ isTopLeft(Δx, Δy)) → hits(P) ≡ 1 (0 seam leaks)

robustness.name: Sampled shared-seam and interior quad stations maintain exact 1-triangle watertight partition

good_fit: Software/compute-shader tile rasterizers, lightmap UV atlas bakers, and visibility buffer generators requiring zero 1-pixel seam cracks
Watertight ray-triangle mesh intersection (Woop et al. 2013) where rays hitting shared edges must never leak through closed manifolds
Explaining why evaluating (P−A)×(B−A) and (P−B)×(A−B) from different origins breaks floating-point antisymmetry
Eliminating per-subtriangle hypot/sqrt calls and collinear square-root cancellation drift (2.17e-8) in barycentric interpolation
not_for: Non-manifold meshes with un-stitched T-junctions where one vertex lies mid-edge of an adjacent triangle
Deliberate wireframe or exploded-view CAD rendering where visible inter-triangle gaps are desired
Neural SDF / Gaussian splat mesh extraction models (NeuS / SuGaR / MeshAnything)
Single isolated triangles with no shared boundary edges or adjacent primitives
